subChunks.title: Comparison Operators
subChunks.hookHtml: Can a program make decisions? Before it can decide, it needs to compare.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Java has six comparison operators that produce a boolean result:

  • == equal to
  • != not equal to
  • < less than
  • > greater than
  • <= less than or equal
  • >= greater than or equal
int age = 18;
System.out.println(age >= 18); // true
System.out.println(age == 21); // false

Important: = is assignment, == is comparison!

storyBeats.text: Before a spell can branch, it must first learn to compare — to weigh one rune against another and declare a truth.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Comparison operators are the eyes of your code. They look at two values and answer a simple question: true or false?

storyBeats.speaker: Comparison example

subChunks.title: If/Else Statements
subChunks.hookHtml: A guardian at the gate checks your level before letting you through. How does code make decisions?
subChunks.explanationHtml:
An if statement runs code only when a condition is true. Chain else if and else for multiple branches.

int temp = 35;
if (temp > 30) {
    System.out.println("Hot");
} else if (temp > 15) {
    System.out.println("Warm");
} else {
    System.out.println("Cold");
}

Only one branch executes — Java checks top to bottom and stops at the first true condition.

storyBeats.text: The branching spell — one of the most fundamental incantations. It lets your code choose a path.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Think of if/else as a crossroads. Your code examines a condition and takes one path or the other — never both.

storyBeats.speaker: If/else example

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml: Check a variable score. Print "A" if >= 90, "B" if >= 80, "C" if >= 70, else "F".
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain if/else to a friend who has never coded. Use a real-world analogy.

questions.questionHtml: What happens if no if/else if condition is true?
questions.explanationHtml: If no condition matches, the else block executes. No else = nothing happens.
15 > 20 is false. 15 > 10 is true → prints "medium". Stops checking.

questions.questionHtml: This always prints "even" no matter what. Find the bug.
questions.correctAnswer: Remove the semicolon after the if condition
questions.explanationHtml: The semicolon after if (...) creates an empty body. The block always runs.

subChunks.title: Logical Operators
subChunks.hookHtml: What if two conditions must both be true? Or if either one is enough?
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Three logical operators:

  • && (AND) — both must be true
  • || (OR) — at least one true
  • ! (NOT) — flips true↔false
boolean hasTicket = true;
boolean isVIP = false;
if (hasTicket && isVIP) {
    System.out.println("VIP entry");
} else if (hasTicket || isVIP) {
    System.out.println("Standard entry");
}

storyBeats.text: Combining conditions is like combining potion ingredients — the right combination unlocks powerful effects.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: AND requires both truths. OR needs only one. NOT inverts. These are the building blocks of all decisions.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml: Check if a user can log in: username equals "admin" AND password equals "secret".
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain &&, ||, and ! operators with a real-world example for each.

questions.explanationHtml: AND (&&) returns true only when both operands are true.

subChunks.title: Switch Statements
subChunks.hookHtml: A menu with 7 options — would you really write 7 else-if branches?
subChunks.explanationHtml:
switch is cleaner than long if/else chains when comparing one value against many options.

int day = 3;
switch (day) {
    case 1: System.out.println("Monday"); break;
    case 2: System.out.println("Tuesday"); break;
    case 3: System.out.println("Wednesday"); break;
    default: System.out.println("Other");
}

Don't forget break! Without it, execution falls through to the next case.

storyBeats.text: When a spell must choose between many distinct forms, switch provides clarity.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: A switch is like a sorting hat — it examines one value and sends execution down the matching path.

subChunks.title: Ternary Operator
subChunks.hookHtml: Can you write an if/else in just one line?
subChunks.explanationHtml:
The ternary operator is shorthand for simple if/else:

// condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse
int age = 20;
String status = (age >= 18) ? "adult" : "minor";

Use it for simple conditions. For complex logic, stick with if/else.

storyBeats.text: The ternary operator — a spell condensed into a single line.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Use it when a full if/else feels like overkill. But never sacrifice clarity for brevity.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml: Use a ternary to find the larger of two numbers and print the result.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the ternary operator. When should you use it vs if/else?

options: if condition then value else value
questions.explanationHtml: The ternary uses ? and : to provide two possible values.
